motion.purpose: Near dust plane: half the mid rate.

components.name: Link Prompt, primary
components.description: The one primary action: caret and label in signal amber. Only the résumé prompt uses it. No hover style of its own; GitHub gives images inside links none.

components.name: Link Prompt
components.description: Default destination prompt: d2 caret, ink label, 2px cells, 24px tall, width to the ink. Sits in one line of prompts separated by  .

components.name: Section Label
components.description: Section heading in label-spaced cells: uppercase head in ink, two blank glyphs of air, '· TAIL' in d2. Lives inside an <h3>.

components.name: Queue Row, front
components.description: Depth 0: ink name at 2.5-cell tracking, amber caret and status, d3 dotted leader that holds still.

components.name: Queue Row, depth 2
components.description: Two steps back: d2 name at 1-cell tracking, d2 caret and status, leader drifting 8px every 2.7s (the near dust plane's speed).

components.name: Queue Row, phone
components.description: 360px phone drawing set 1:1: name in 3px cells with the rank's tracking, status under it in 2px cells, no leader.

components.name: Title-screen Headline
components.description: The hero headline at phone size (5px cells) with the blinking amber caret and the far dust plane drifting behind; dust thinned for the panel. Dark only: phosphor grain plus a 25% blurred bleed.

components.name: Signal, NO SIGNAL failure
components.description: The only reversed cell in the system: 'NO SIGNAL' knocked out of an ink block so the void shows through the letters. Drawn when the 52-week total is zero; phone layout shown.

components.name: Greetings Scroller
components.description: The closing cracktro scroller and the only type that travels: d2 label cells, two copies end to end, about 42px/s. Text shortened for the panel.

narrative.overview:
Raj Patel's GitHub profile is drawn as a demoscene title screen. One hand-drawn bitmap face rides its baselines over a void that is GitHub's own ground: every drawing is a transparent SVG, so the page behind it is the screen. In the dark theme the type is phosphor ivory with a faint bleed of light; in the light theme the same drawing prints in inverse video, ink on paper, with no glow. Behind the type, square dust motes drift in up to three planes, gathered into swept ribbons. In front, nothing travels except a blinking caret and, at the foot of the page, the closing greetings scroller.

Shipped work is a worked queue, and rank is depth. The front row is the brightest, the widest tracked, amber-marked and still; each row behind it steps down one brightness, tightens its tracking and lets its dotted leader drift faster, the way far layers move fastest in a parallax starfield. One signal amber is spent only where a visitor should act or where something is live. Nothing is enclosed by a rule or a box; the only filled cell behind a letter is a reversed cell, and it means failure.

The platform sets the edges. GitHub sanitises README HTML (no CSS, no JS), so every custom visual is an SVG image inside a `<picture>` that picks a theme pair and, under 600px, a dedicated 360px phone drawing set 1:1. Links inside an SVG do not work, so every link is markdown or an `<a>` around a picture. GitHub's own sans sets the markdown copy between the drawings and is never imitated inside them.
keyCharacteristics: One bitmap face (5×7 on a 5×9 cell grid), drawn as merged pixel runs at 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10px cells.
Transparent void; four text brightness steps per theme plus one dust step; one signal amber.
Rank is depth: brightness, tracking and leader drift move together.
Up to three dust planes: the rear plane drifts fastest, each step forward halves the rate, the type plane is still.
No rules, no boxes, no radius, no shadows; a reversed cell means failure.
Wide drawings at 830px, phone drawings at 360px set 1:1, switched at a 600px viewport.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Signal amber is spent on three things only: the primary action, the front row of the queue, and live markers. A second amber element anywhere else dilutes the one place a visitor should act.

rules.name: The Transparent Void Rule
rules.body: No SVG paints a background. GitHub's ground is the screen, in both themes; the reversed failure cell is the only fill that sits behind letters.

rules.name: The Dust Is Not Ink Rule
rules.body: d3 never carries a letter. It is reserved for motes and leader dots, so anything set in it reads as atmosphere, not information.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Every drawn letter and symbol is the bitmap face, drawn as path runs. No second typeface, no `<text>`, no embedded font, and no imitation of GitHub's sans inside a drawing.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: No text cell renders below 2px. A drawing that would shrink a 2px cell on a phone gets its own 360px drawing set 1:1; drawings narrow enough to fit (link prompts up to 132px, labels up to 320px) stay at native size everywhere.

rules.name: The Lowercase Voice Rule
rules.body: Statements and values speak lowercase ("i build ai", "open to ai roles + freelance", "in production"). Uppercase belongs to the masthead name, the ID line, the keys STATUS and NOW, and section labels.

rules.name: The Narrow Drawing Rule
rules.body: A phone never sees a wide drawing scaled down. Every drawing wider than 360px has a 360px twin set 1:1 that drops dust planes and leaders but keeps brightness steps and tracking.

rules.name: The One-Line Picture Rule
rules.body: One `` per line, sources in the order narrow-dark, narrow, dark, then the light ``. No line breaks or indentation inside it.

rules.name: The Rank Is Depth Rule
rules.body: Rank is shown by brightness step, tracking and leader drift together, never by one lever alone and never by size, weight or a badge. All four rows share one cell size.

rules.name: The Halving Rule
rules.body: The rear plane drifts fastest, and each step forward halves the rate, down to the front plane, which never moves. Type is that front plane: only the caret blinks, and only the closing scroller travels.

rules.name: The Inverse Video Rule
rules.body: The light theme is the same drawing in inverse video: identical geometry, counts and motion, with the ladder inverted from ink-on-night to ink-on-paper. The phosphor bleed exists only in the dark.

rules.name: The No-Enclosure Rule
rules.body: Nothing is enclosed by a rule, a border, a box or a frame. A dotted leader connects a name to its status and stops 16px short of both; it never spans the column or underlines a heading. The signal draws no axis or baseline: quiet days settle as loose motes.

rules.name: The Square Mark Rule
rules.body: Every mark is a filled, axis-aligned square or rectangle. A new mark is built from cells, not drawn as a stroke or a curve.

dos: **Do** spend signal amber only on the `> résumé` prompt, the front queue row's caret and status, and live markers (masthead block, status bars, hero caret, signal sync square, signal now-bar, busiest-day motes).
**Do** give every drawing wider than 360px a 360px `-narrow` twin set 1:1, so every drawing ships as four files: `-dark`, `-light`, `-narrow-dark`, `-narrow-light`.
**Do** write each `` on one line, with sources in the order narrow-dark, narrow, dark, then the light `` carrying the alt text.
**Do** show rank with all three levers at once: brightness step (ink, d1, d2, rear), tracking (2.5, 1.75, 1, 0.5 cells) and leader drift (still, 5.4s, 2.7s, 1.35s per 8px).
**Do** keep dust behind type in at most three planes, rear fastest and halving at each step forward; phone drawings keep the far plane only.
**Do** draw every letter and symbol in the bitmap face at a 2px cell or larger, adding missing glyphs to `_SPEC` in its 5-wide grammar.
**Do** keep every SVG transparent, with `role="img"`, a title, and the reduced-motion guard on anything that moves.
**Do** put links on the `<a>` around a picture or in markdown beside it.
**Do** regenerate instead of hand-editing: `python3 scripts/build_assets.py` and `python3 scripts/signal.py`.
**Do** mark failure with a reversed glyph cell, and use a reversed cell for nothing else.
donts: **Don't** enclose anything in a rule, border, box, frame or card, and don't separate sections with `<hr>` or `---`; leaders stop 16px short of the name and the status.
**Don't** paint a background into any SVG; GitHub's ground is the void in both themes.
**Don't** set a letter in d3, or anything except the rearmost queue row in rear.
**Don't** let a phone scale a wide drawing down, or let any text cell render below 2px.
**Don't** add a second typeface, a `<text>` element or an embedded font to a drawing, and don't imitate GitHub's sans inside one.
**Don't** move type: no drifting, bouncing or fading letters, and no leader on the front row. The caret blinks and the closing scroller travels; nothing else in the type plane moves.
**Don't** add glow, blur or shadow beyond the dark hero headline's phosphor bleed; the light theme has none.
**Don't** round a corner or draw a stroke or a curve; marks are filled squares and rectangles.
**Don't** add third-party stats cards, badges, shields or emoji; the signal is the only data graphic, and it is drawn in dust.
**Don't** put a link inside an SVG; GitHub drops it.
**Don't** edit, move, reformat or print the hidden part's layers: the README's second HTML comment and the dark hero's XML comment generated from `NOTE`.
